sections.markdown:
## C — Before you drive: required working equipment, tire checks, the safety belt law, child restraints and air bags, travel information, vehicle upkeep, secured loads and brakes
Knowledge domain: what must work on a vehicle before it is driven, the quick tire checks Arizona's climate calls for, who must wear a belt, how young children must ride, where to get road information, and the basic upkeep, load and brake rules for every vehicle.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Your vehicle may not have defective or missing equipment, and the brakes, speedometer, turn signals, horn and emergency flashers must all be in working order. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
The windshield must be intact, the tires in good condition, the seat belts working, and the driver and front passenger side windows operational. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Before starting the vehicle, adjust your seat, the steering wheel, and the rearview and outside mirrors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Before putting the vehicle in motion, check that the turn signals and brakes work. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Arizona's extremes — intense summer heat, summer monsoon storms, and winter snow and ice in the high country — make tire maintenance especially important. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
A free inspection from a tire professional, which many offer, is the best way to make sure your tires can handle Arizona conditions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
To check tire pressure, find your vehicle's recommended psi, usually on the door jamb, read the tire with a pressure gauge, and add or release air as needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
For the penny test, put Lincoln's head into a groove where the tread looks lowest; if no part of his head is covered by tread, it may be time for new tires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
Every front seat occupant must wear the lap and shoulder belt, properly adjusted and fastened, whenever the vehicle is moving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
Where only a lap belt is installed at a seat, that lap belt must be properly adjusted and fastened while the vehicle is moving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
The driver must make every passenger under 16 buckle up. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
A combined lap and shoulder belt greatly cuts your chance of serious injury in a crash, and the lap belt keeps you from being thrown out of the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
The shoulder belt stops your head and chest from hitting the dashboard or windshield. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
In vehicles with an automatic shoulder belt and a manual lap belt, buckling the lap belt is extremely important. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
Seat belts are not designed for children, and Arizona law forbids driving on state highways with a child under 5 who is not properly secured in a child restraint system. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
Children aged 5 to 8 must stay in a child restraint system until they are at least 4 feet 9 inches tall. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
The manual asks anyone who sees an unrestrained child in a moving vehicle to report the plate number, city and the child's location to its child-safety hotline. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
A driver carrying more than one child under 8 must secure as many of them in child restraints as is reasonable for the size of the passenger area and the number of passengers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
Child restraint systems must meet United States Department of Transportation safety standards and be used according to both the seat maker's and the vehicle maker's instructions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
Air bags save lives but are unsafe for children under 12, and children 12 and under should never ride in the front seat. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
If a child must ride in front, turn off the passenger-side air bag, which most newer vehicles allow with an on/off switch. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
The Arizona Governor's Office of Highway Safety is the contact for more information on safety issues, online at azgohs.gov. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A02
Dialing 511 at any time, day or night, gives up-to-the-minute reports on traffic conditions and road closures, transit and airports. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
The 511 service also reports on tourism, metro-region quick reports, and construction and work zones. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
On a 511 call, pressing the star key switches to touch-tone mode, or you can use voice prompts by listening to the whole introduction and cutting background noise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
Travel information is also online at az511.com, and both 511 and az511.com are free services from the Arizona Department of Transportation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
Drivers are responsible for making sure the vehicle they drive is safe, and an unsafe vehicle costs more to run than a maintained one. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
A vehicle in good condition gives you an extra margin of safety when you need it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
If your vehicle fails a required emission inspection at an authorized station, you get 30 days to fix the problem and return for a follow-up emission re-check. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A03
Follow the owner's manual for routine maintenance; some tasks you can do yourself, while others need a qualified technician. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A03
Arizona law (A.R.S. 28-1098.A) bars driving or moving a vehicle on a road unless it is built or loaded so none of its load can drop, sift, leak or otherwise escape. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A03
Every motor vehicle must have brakes in good working condition, and cars and trucks need both a foot brake and a parking brake. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A03
Each set of brakes on a car or truck must work on at least two wheels, and a motorcycle needs at least one brake applied by hand or foot. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A03
Each front seat occupant of a motor vehicle made after 1972 must have a seat belt fastened and adjusted. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0021]

Misconceptions: a lap belt alone is not a reason to skip buckling where that is all the seat has — it must still be fastened; reaching age five does not end child-seat use, the height rule continues until eight; a child in the front seat is not made safe by the air bag, it should be switched off; checking signals and brakes comes before the vehicle moves, not after the first stop.
Mnemonics: Seat, Wheel, Mirrors, then Signals and Brakes — adjust first, test before rolling; for tread, Lincoln's head should be partly hidden.
Glossary: psi means pounds per square inch, the unit for tire pressure; child restraint system means a car seat or booster that meets federal safety standards; emission inspection means the exhaust test some Arizona vehicles must pass; az511.com means the free ADOT travel-information website.
Dynamic facts: the child-safety hotline, the highway safety office phone numbers and the travel-information phone menu features are contact and service details that can change; the manual says only that a vehicle may need an emission inspection without saying which vehicles do, so check with ADOT for your own vehicle.
